front: In Okta's 'as a Source' feature, what does mastering an attribute 'as a Source' from a downstream app mean?
back: Okta reads that attribute's value out of the app during import and can push it into the user's Okta profile (and optionally other apps), rather than the app always taking its value from Okta — a two-way rather than Okta-mastered relationship for that attribute.

front: What is profile source priority in Okta, and why does the priority list order matter?
back: When more than one source (HR system, AD, LDAP, custom app) is authorized to master the same attribute, Okta's priority list decides which source wins on conflict — the first authoritative source in the list for that attribute overwrites values from sources listed after it during each import/sync.

front: Name two things to validate before promoting an advanced sourcing configuration from test to production.
back: That attribute mappings/transformations produce expected values on a representative sample of real records, and that import/sync doesn't silently overwrite attributes still mastered by another authoritative source (a source priority conflict).

front: What is a common architecture pattern for combining HR-as-a-Source with an AD import in the same org?
back: HR masters identity lifecycle attributes (name, title, department, employment status) and triggers provisioning; AD continues to master AD-specific attributes and remains the source for on-prem app authentication, with source priority resolving any overlap.

front: What data migration strategy consideration is unique to advanced sourcing versus a simple single-source import?
back: Sequencing which source imports first so matching rules (e.g. by email or employee ID) correctly link existing Okta profiles to the right downstream records, avoiding duplicate user creation when multiple sources are turned on close together.

front: What is an attribute transformation in the context of profile mappings?
back: A mapping-level function (string concatenation, case conversion, an Okta Expression Language expression) applied while pushing a source value into a target profile attribute, reshaping data instead of copying it verbatim.

front: Why would a consultant configure an app as an authoritative 'source' rather than just a provisioning target?
back: When that app is the true system of record for certain user data (e.g. a specialized HR or contractor-management tool) and Okta profile fields should reflect edits made there rather than only push data outward to it.

front: What's the first troubleshooting step when an advanced sourcing sync applies unexpected attribute values to profiles?
back: Check the source priority order and each source's individual attribute-level mapping settings — most unexpected overwrites trace back to a higher-priority source pushing a value the admin didn't expect for that attribute.

front: Can profile source priority be set per-attribute rather than only per-source overall?
back: Yes — Okta's profile source priority lets you designate, attribute by attribute, an ordered list of which authoritative sources may write that specific attribute, not just one blanket source ranking for the whole profile.

front: What deployment consideration matters most rolling out advanced sourcing across a large or phased population?
back: Testing sourcing/mapping configuration against a pilot group first, monitoring for unintended attribute overwrites or provisioning errors, before expanding source priority rules and imports to the full population.

front: What problem does Okta Access Gateway (OAG) solve?
back: It extends Okta SSO and adaptive access policies to on-premises and legacy web applications that don't natively support modern federation protocols, acting as a reverse proxy that enforces Okta authentication in front of the legacy app.

front: In OAuth 2.0, what is the difference between the 'resource owner' and 'client' roles?
back: The resource owner is the user/entity who owns the protected data and can grant access to it; the client is the application requesting access to that data on the resource owner's behalf — these are never the same role even when a user is using the client app directly.

front: What is the primary use case for Okta's RADIUS Agent?
back: It lets legacy on-prem infrastructure and network devices that only support RADIUS authentication (VPNs, older network gear) authenticate against Okta, bridging RADIUS requests to Okta's cloud directory.

front: What OIDC flow is recommended for a single-page application that cannot securely store a client secret?
back: Authorization Code flow with PKCE — it avoids exposing a client secret in the browser while still protecting the authorization code exchange from interception.

front: What does 'Advanced Server Access' primarily secure?
back: SSH and RDP access to Linux/Windows servers, applying short-lived, ephemeral certificates and Okta-based identity instead of long-lived static credentials or shared SSH keys.

front: When troubleshooting a failed advanced SAML integration, what artifact should you inspect first?
back: The SAML response/assertion itself (via a browser SAML tracer or the app's debug logs) to check its status code, NameID format, and attribute statements against what the service provider expects.

front: What does the OIDC 'implicit' flow return directly in the redirect URI, and why is it discouraged today?
back: It returns the ID token (and sometimes access token) directly in the URL fragment with no server-side code exchange; discouraged because tokens are exposed in browser history/logs and no client secret can be used, making Authorization Code + PKCE the modern replacement.

front: What commonly causes SAML assertion signature validation failures in an advanced SSO integration?
back: A mismatch between the signing certificate configured in Okta and the certificate the service provider has on file — often after a certificate rotation on one side wasn't updated on the other.

front: What distinguishes an 'advanced SAML implementation scenario' from a basic SAML app setup?
back: Custom attribute statements, signed and encrypted assertions, non-standard NameID formats, IdP- vs SP-initiated flow requirements, or multiple SAML apps chained through routing/discovery — beyond the out-of-the-box OIN wizard defaults.

front: What is the client_credentials OAuth 2.0 grant type used for?
back: Machine-to-machine (service-to-service) authorization with no end user involved — the client authenticates with its own credentials to obtain an access token scoped to its own permissions.

front: Why configure the RADIUS Agent with a shared secret and a network device IP allowlist?
back: To ensure only trusted, known network devices can submit RADIUS authentication requests to the agent, since RADIUS traffic has no strong built-in mutual authentication beyond the shared secret and source validation.

front: What's a key redundancy consideration deploying Okta Access Gateway in production?
back: Deploying multiple OAG instances behind a load balancer so legacy app access doesn't go down if a single gateway instance fails or needs maintenance.

front: What does the OAuth 2.0 'scope' parameter control?
back: The specific set of permissions/resources the client is requesting on the resource owner's behalf — the authorization server and resource owner use scopes to limit what an issued access token can actually be used for.

front: What does a 'clock skew' error between Okta and a service provider usually indicate?
back: The SP's server clock and Okta's issued assertion timestamps (NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter) are too far apart, causing the SP to reject an otherwise valid assertion as expired or not-yet-valid — usually fixed by correcting NTP sync on the SP side.

front: What advantage does Authorization Code flow have over Implicit flow for a traditional server-side web app?
back: Access/ID tokens are exchanged directly between the app's backend and Okta's token endpoint over a secure channel, never passing through the browser, and a client secret can authenticate that exchange.

front: Why would an org choose Okta RADIUS Agent over migrating a device to SAML/OIDC directly?
back: The device or infrastructure (older VPN concentrators, network switches) only supports RADIUS and can't be upgraded or replaced soon, so RADIUS Agent bridges it to centralize authentication through Okta anyway.

front: What does Advanced Server Access's short-lived certificate authentication eliminate?
back: The risk of long-lived SSH keys or shared credentials being copied, leaked, or left valid indefinitely — certificates are issued per-session and expire quickly, tying access back to a verified Okta identity each time.

front: A SAML app works IdP-initiated but fails SP-initiated (or vice versa) — what does that suggest?
back: The two flows exercise different code paths (e.g. RelayState handling, ACS URL matching, AuthnRequest signature validation) — a failure isolated to one direction usually points to a misconfiguration specific to that flow's validation path.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What is the Okta Provisioning Platform (OPP)?
back: Okta's underlying framework for provisioning connectors (OIN-built and custom SCIM/API-based) that governs how user lifecycle events — create, update, deactivate — are pushed out to downstream applications.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What is the difference between an Okta Inline Hook and an Event Hook?
back: An Inline Hook is called synchronously during an Okta process (token issuance, import, password validation) and its response can alter that process's outcome; an Event Hook is called asynchronously after an event already happened, purely to notify an external system, and cannot change what occurred.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: Give an example use case for a Token Inline Hook.
back: Injecting a custom claim into an OIDC ID or access token at issuance time by calling out to an external system, e.g. adding a computed entitlement value not stored in the Okta profile.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What is a Custom URL Domain used for in Okta?
back: Replacing the default okta.com-branded sign-in URL with the organization's own domain (e.g. login.company.com) so the authentication experience feels fully white-labeled.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What is required before Okta can send mail from a Custom Email Domain instead of the default Okta-branded sender?
back: The organization must add and verify specific DNS records (SPF/DKIM/CNAME-style) proving domain ownership and enabling Okta to send authenticated mail as that domain.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What does the SCIM App Wizard let an admin configure without writing a full custom connector?
back: A SCIM 2.0-compliant provisioning integration by supplying the target app's base URL, authentication method, and supported schema/attributes through a guided UI, rather than hand-building a bespoke API connector.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What is 'MFA as a Service' referring to among Okta's custom configuration options?
back: Using Okta's Authentication API/SDKs to embed Okta's MFA factor enrollment and verification directly into a custom-built application's own UI, rather than redirecting to Okta's hosted sign-in widget.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What is a Registration Inline Hook typically used for?
back: Running custom validation or enrichment logic (checking an external eligibility list, generating a custom user ID) during Okta's self-service registration flow, before the new account is finalized.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: Why might an org need both a Custom URL Domain and a Custom Email Domain?
back: Custom URL Domain brands the sign-in/hosted pages users interact with, while Custom Email Domain brands the sender address of transactional emails — they solve different parts of white-labeling and are configured independently.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What is the Okta Authentication API primarily used for, distinct from OIDC/OAuth endpoints?
back: Driving a fully custom-built sign-in experience (username/password submission, MFA challenge/response, session token retrieval) directly against Okta's API rather than redirecting to Okta's hosted Sign-In Widget.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What's the tradeoff between the hosted Sign-In Widget and a custom Authentication API integration?
back: The hosted widget requires far less engineering effort and stays current with new Okta security features automatically, while a custom Authentication API build gives full UI control but puts the burden of correctly handling every MFA/session edge case on the org's own code.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What might a SAML Assertion Inline Hook call out to?
back: A third-party service that computes a custom attribute value or claim to include in the outgoing SAML assertion at generation time, based on real-time logic that can't be pre-computed and stored in the Okta profile.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: In the Okta Provisioning Platform, what determines whether a downstream app receives a deactivate call when a user is removed?
back: Whether the provisioning integration for that app has the 'Deactivate Users' provisioning feature enabled and mapped, and whether the user was actively provisioned to that app in the first place.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: Why recommend the SCIM App Wizard over a manual API-based custom app integration?
back: When the target app already exposes a standards-compliant SCIM 2.0 endpoint, the wizard gets provisioning working faster and with less custom code than writing a bespoke integration against the app's proprietary REST API.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What DNS record type most commonly needs to be added for Custom URL Domain verification?
back: A CNAME record pointing the custom subdomain at Okta's provided target hostname, alongside a TXT record for domain ownership verification.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What's a practical risk of over-relying on Inline Hooks for critical authentication logic?
back: If the external endpoint the hook calls is slow or unavailable, Okta's default hook timeout can fail or delay the entire authentication/provisioning flow for real users, so hook endpoints need to be highly available and fast.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What does Okta's Authentication API expose that the hosted Sign-In Widget's default config doesn't easily allow?
back: Fully custom UI/UX and branding for every step of the login and MFA process, including embedding sign-in inline within a native mobile app screen rather than a browser redirect.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What's an operational risk of Custom Email Domain misconfiguration?
back: If SPF/DKIM records aren't set up correctly, transactional Okta emails (password resets, activation links) sent from the custom domain may be flagged as spam or rejected outright by recipient mail servers.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What is the role of an Import Inline Hook?
back: It runs during a scheduled or manual import job, letting an external system transform or validate incoming user attribute values before they're written into Okta profiles.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: Can the SCIM App Wizard support custom attributes beyond SCIM's core schema?
back: Yes — it supports extending the base SCIM schema with custom attributes as long as the target app's SCIM endpoint also implements and returns them, mapped through Okta's Profile Editor like any other app attribute.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What's the Okta Provisioning Platform's relationship to the OIN (Okta Integration Network)?
back: Most OIN-listed provisioning integrations are themselves built on OPP's connector framework — OPP is the underlying engine, while OIN is the catalog/wizard experience admins use to configure a specific app's connector.

domain: Implementing Custom Configuration Options with Okta
front: What should a consultant verify before enabling a Password Import Inline Hook?
back: That the external system truly is the authoritative source of legacy password hashes/verification logic, and its endpoint reliably returns a fast pass/fail response, since this hook sits directly in the critical path of every affected user's login attempt.

front: In a multi-domain AD forest, what must be true for one Okta AD agent instance to see users across all domains?
back: The agent's service account needs appropriate read (and if configured, write-back) permissions replicated/trusted across every domain in the forest, since one agent installation can be configured to monitor multiple domains within a forest.

front: What is DSSO (Agentless Desktop SSO) in Okta?
back: A feature letting domain-joined Windows devices authenticate to Okta silently using their existing Kerberos ticket from AD, without prompting for credentials again, and without a separate on-prem DSSO agent install.

front: What network requirement is typically needed for Agentless DSSO to function?
back: The user's browser must reach Okta's DSSO endpoint from within the corporate network (or a trusted VPN) so Kerberos negotiation can complete, and the browser must trust the Okta domain for integrated Windows authentication.

front: What's the core difference between Okta's LDAP Agent integration and its AD agent integration?
back: The LDAP Agent integrates with any LDAPv3-compliant directory using LDAP-specific schema mapping and bind credentials, while the AD agent is purpose-built for AD's specific schema, group model, and domain/forest trust structure.

front: What is the 'LDAP Interface' feature used for?
back: Exposing Okta's own universal directory to legacy applications that can only authenticate against an LDAP directory, letting those apps bind/query Okta as if it were a standard LDAP server.

front: In a multi-forest AD environment with no trust between forests, what does a consultant typically need to configure?
back: A separate AD agent (or agent group) per forest, since an agent authenticates and queries within the trust boundary of the domain/forest it's installed in and can't traverse into an untrusted forest.

front: Why might Agentless DSSO fail on a personal/unmanaged device even if it works on corporate laptops?
back: The device isn't domain-joined and has no valid Kerberos ticket for the corporate AD domain, so there's no ticket for Okta's DSSO endpoint to validate — the user falls back to standard username/password sign-in.

front: What determines which attributes sync into a user's Okta profile via the LDAP Agent?
back: The LDAP schema discovery/mapping step during agent setup, where the admin maps LDAP attribute names to Okta profile attributes similarly to AD attribute mapping.

front: AD agent-based import suddenly stops picking up new users in one OU — what's the first troubleshooting step?
back: Verify the agent's configured import base DN/OU scope still includes that OU and that the service account still has read permission on it — OU-level permission or scope changes are a frequent cause of a silent partial-import failure.

front: What's a key security consideration exposing Okta via the LDAP Interface to legacy apps?
back: LDAP bind traffic is often unencrypted or weakly encrypted by legacy clients, so the interface should be configured to require LDAPS (LDAP over TLS) wherever the legacy client supports it, avoiding credential exposure in transit.

front: Does Agentless DSSO require installing software on the domain-joined endpoint itself?
back: No — that's the defining difference from the older agent-based DSSO approach; agentless DSSO relies entirely on the browser's native Kerberos/SPNEGO support and IWA configuration rather than an installed endpoint agent.

front: What happens to nested AD security groups when imported into Okta via the AD agent?
back: Okta flattens nested group membership during import — a user who is a member of a group only through another group's membership is still recognized as an effective member of the top-level group in Okta.

front: Would a consultant recommend the LDAP Agent for a directory that is technically Active Directory, rather than the dedicated AD agent?
back: Generally no — the AD agent's purpose-built schema/group handling is a better fit for AD specifically; the LDAP Agent is reserved for non-AD or generic LDAPv3 directories where the AD-specific agent doesn't apply.

front: What should be verified on the firewall side before deploying an on-prem AD or LDAP agent?
back: That the agent host can make outbound connections to Okta's cloud service over HTTPS (443) — Okta agents never require inbound firewall rules, since all agent-initiated connections are outbound-only for security.

front: What limitation should a consultant flag about the LDAP Interface for write operations from legacy apps?
back: Its support for write operations back into Okta's universal directory is more limited than native Okta APIs/SCIM, so it's best positioned as a read/bind authentication bridge rather than a full read-write LDAP replacement.

front: Why does attribute mapping consistency across AD agent instances matter in a multi-domain/multi-forest deployment?
back: If different agents map the same logical attribute (e.g. department) differently across domains, users imported from different domains end up with inconsistent Okta profile data, breaking downstream group rules or app assignments that depend on that attribute.

front: What does 'inbound federation' mean in the context of Okta?
back: Configuring Okta itself as the Service Provider (SP) that trusts and accepts authentication assertions from an external Identity Provider (IdP) — the reverse of Okta acting as the IdP for downstream apps.

front: What is IdP Discovery used for?
back: Automatically routing a user to the correct Identity Provider (Okta itself, a social IdP, or a third-party inbound federation IdP) based on rules like email domain or network zone, before the user manually picks or types credentials.

front: What is an IdP routing rule evaluated against?
back: Conditions such as the user's identifier (e.g. email domain pattern), the requesting application, device/network context, or group membership — the first matching rule determines which configured IdP the user is routed to.

front: What is 'account linking' in an inbound federation context?
back: Matching an incoming federated identity (from a social or third-party IdP) to an existing Okta user record — automatically by a matching attribute like email, or via a manual confirmation step — so the same person doesn't end up with duplicate Okta accounts.

front: What is Okta Org2Org used for?
back: Federating identities and enabling SSO between two separate Okta orgs (e.g. after an acquisition, or between a parent/subsidiary org), letting a user authenticate in one Okta org and access resources managed by another Okta org.

front: Name two examples of Social Identity Providers Okta commonly supports for inbound federation.
back: Google and Facebook are two of Okta's most common built-in Social IdP options (others include Microsoft, LinkedIn, and Apple), letting end users authenticate with an existing consumer account instead of an Okta-managed password.

front: Authentication succeeds at the external IdP but the user is denied at Okta — what's the frequent root cause?
back: Account linking/JIT provisioning misconfiguration — Okta received a valid assertion but couldn't match or create a corresponding Okta user record, often due to a missing or mismatched matching attribute (like email).

front: What does it mean for Okta to act as a Service Provider (SP) to a third-party IdP?
back: Okta receives and validates SAML or OIDC authentication assertions issued by an external identity provider and, on success, establishes an Okta session for that user — inbound federation, as opposed to Okta's more common outbound IdP role.

front: Why configure IdP Discovery routing rules by network zone rather than only by email domain?
back: To force users on the untrusted/external network to always go through stronger inbound federation or MFA-enforcing IdPs, while allowing a lighter-weight or different IdP path from a trusted corporate network zone.

front: In Okta Org2Org, which org's policies typically govern the user during initial authentication?
back: Generally the org where the user's authoritative account lives enforces its own policies during initial authentication, while the target (resource) org's app assignments and access policies still govern what the user can do once federated in.

front: What troubleshooting artifact is most useful when an inbound federation SAML assertion is rejected by Okta?
back: The System Log entry for the failed login event, which typically records the specific reason (signature validation failure, missing required attribute, clock skew) Okta rejected the incoming assertion.

front: What's the key difference between automatic and manual account linking during inbound federation?
back: Automatic linking matches and links accounts silently based on a trusted matching attribute (e.g. verified email) with no user interaction; manual linking prompts the user to confirm or enter existing Okta credentials first, adding verification when automatic matching isn't safe enough.

front: What happens if no configured IdP Discovery routing rule matches the incoming request?
back: It falls through to a default action/IdP defined in the policy (commonly Okta's own org as the default IdP), ensuring every request has a deterministic destination even when no specific rule applies.

front: What common use case drives an organization to adopt Okta Org2Org rather than a full org merge?
back: A merger/acquisition or franchise-style structure where each entity needs to keep operating its own independent Okta org (own admins, own policies) while still allowing seamless cross-org SSO access for shared applications or staff.

front: Beyond enabling a Social IdP in Okta, what detail must be confirmed before go-live?
back: That the correct OAuth application/client ID and secret have been registered with the social provider's own developer console, with the exact redirect URI Okta expects — a mismatch here is a very common cause of social login failing in production.

front: How does inbound federation troubleshooting differ from standard outbound SAML app troubleshooting?
back: The consultant must inspect the AuthnRequest and assertion validation rules on Okta's Identity Provider configuration (as the relying party/SP), rather than a downstream app's SP configuration — the roles are reversed, so the fix is often in Okta's IdP settings.

front: What is Okta FastPass?
back: A phishing-resistant authentication factor built into the Okta Verify app that uses device-bound cryptographic keys and device signals (management state, OS security posture) to authenticate a user without a shared secret or push-approval interaction, when device assurance conditions are met.

front: What does Global Session Policy control versus an app-specific Authentication Policy?
back: Global Session Policy governs org-wide sign-in requirements and session behavior (session lifetime, primary factor requirements) applied before any specific app is reached; Authentication Policies are then evaluated per-application on top of the already-established session.

front: How does Behavioral Detection integrate with Global Session Policy?
back: Behavioral Detection signals (impossible travel, new device, new IP, new location, new sign-in behavior) can be referenced as conditions within Global Session Policy rules to trigger a step-up requirement, rather than as a standalone deny mechanism.

front: What is the Pre-Authentication Sign-On Evaluation Policy used for?
back: Evaluating and potentially blocking or challenging a sign-in attempt based on network/device risk signals before the user's primary credential is even validated, filtering malicious traffic earlier in the flow.

front: What is ThreatInsight, and what action can it take?
back: An Okta security feature that identifies and can automatically block credential-stuffing and other malicious authentication requests based on IP reputation and observed attack patterns across Okta's global customer base, before those requests reach an org's authentication policies.

front: Can Behavioral Detection alone deny a user's access outright?
back: No — by itself it can only trigger additional verification (step-up authentication); an outright deny requires it to be combined with another enforcement mechanism, such as a policy rule explicitly configured to deny on that risk condition.

front: What are the two primary enforcement modes ThreatInsight supports?
back: 'Log and Allow' (record suspicious requests for visibility but don't block) and 'Log and Enforce' (actively deny suspicious/malicious requests), letting admins start conservatively and tighten enforcement later.

front: What is an Authentication Policy rule's basic anatomy?
back: A set of conditions (user/group membership, network zone, device state, risk signals) paired with an action/requirement (which factors are needed, whether to allow, deny, or require step-up) — rules are evaluated top-to-bottom and the first match applies.

front: What is the 'Catch-All' rule in an Authentication Policy?
back: The final rule in the policy's evaluation order that matches any request not caught by a more specific rule above it, ensuring every authentication attempt has a defined outcome.

front: How does FastPass's device assurance evaluation relate to Okta Verify?
back: Okta Verify is the client that reports the device signals (OS version, disk encryption, screen lock, management status) FastPass evaluates against a configured Device Assurance Policy before issuing its phishing-resistant authentication.

front: What kind of signal does Pre-Authentication Sign-On Evaluation Policy inspect that a standard Authentication Policy does not?
back: Network/IP-level risk signals evaluated before credentials are submitted, versus Authentication Policy which evaluates conditions tied to an already-initiated sign-in attempt.

front: Why place the strictest Authentication Policy rule near the top rather than the bottom of the rule list?
back: Rules are evaluated top-to-bottom and the first matching rule wins — placing a strict rule below a broader permissive rule means the broader rule would match first and the strict rule would never apply.

front: What does it mean that ThreatInsight operates 'across Okta's global customer base'?
back: It aggregates malicious IP/request signals observed across all Okta orgs, so a new attack pattern seen against one org can help protect other orgs before that same source targets them.

front: What session-level setting is typically configured in Global Session Policy rather than an app-specific Authentication Policy?
back: Overall session lifetime and persistent session cookie behavior (how long a session stays valid org-wide before requiring re-authentication), since that governs the org-wide session rather than any single app's access requirement.

front: Why combine Behavioral Detection step-up AND a Device Assurance requirement on the same rule?
back: They evaluate different risk dimensions (behavioral/context anomaly vs. device security posture) — combining both means a request must pass both checks, closing gaps a single-signal policy would miss.

front: What happens during FastPass authentication if the device fails its assigned Device Assurance check?
back: FastPass fails to satisfy the policy rule requiring that device assurance level, and the user is typically redirected to an alternate, usually weaker or more effortful, authentication method per the policy's fallback rule.

front: What's the effect of a Pre-Authentication Sign-On Evaluation Policy rule set to deny based on network zone?
back: Requests from that network zone are blocked before any credential is evaluated, reducing load from unwanted sources and preventing credential-guessing attempts from ever reaching the login form.

front: What's the evaluation order between Pre-Authentication Sign-On Evaluation Policy, Global Session Policy, and Authentication Policy?
back: Pre-Authentication Sign-On Evaluation Policy runs first (before credentials), Global Session Policy establishes org-wide sign-in/session requirements next, and app-specific Authentication Policy is evaluated last as the user attempts to access a specific application.

front: What is Okta's 'API Code Collection'?
back: A library of ready-made, example API scripts/snippets published by Okta covering common administrative tasks (bulk user operations, reporting, custom automation), meant to be adapted rather than written from scratch.

front: What HTTP authentication method does a typical scripted call to the Okta Management API use?
back: An SSWS API token (or, increasingly, an OAuth 2.0 access token via API Access Management/service app) passed in the Authorization header, rather than basic username/password credentials.

front: Why is pagination important to handle correctly in scripted Okta API calls that list users or apps?
back: Okta's list endpoints return results in pages with a Link header for the next page — a script that ignores pagination and only reads the first page will silently miss records once an org's user/app count exceeds the page size.

front: What's a best practice for handling Okta API rate limits in a scripted bulk operation?
back: Read the returned rate-limit headers (remaining calls, reset time) and implement backoff/retry logic rather than firing requests as fast as possible, since exceeding limits results in 429 responses and possible temporary throttling.

front: What advantage does an OAuth 2.0 access token (service app + scopes) have over a static SSWS API token for automation?
back: Scoped, short-lived tokens tied to specific granted permissions reduce blast radius if leaked, and access can be revoked/rotated per-integration without needing to regenerate a single shared admin token used by many scripts.

front: What's a common use case in Okta's API Code Collection for the Users API?
back: Bulk user deactivation, bulk password reset triggers, or exporting a full user roster with custom attributes for reporting — repetitive admin tasks not efficiently done one-by-one through the admin console UI.

front: Why should a scripted integration request the narrowest scopes it needs rather than a broad admin-equivalent scope?
back: Limiting scope reduces the damage an exposed token/credential could cause and follows least-privilege — a reporting script, for example, should only get read scopes, never write/admin scopes it doesn't use.

front: What response detail should a script always check, not just assume success from a 2xx status?
back: The response body's actual returned object/fields, since some bulk or async operations return 200/202 immediately while the actual work (e.g. an async export job) completes later — scripts need to poll or handle async job status separately.

front: What's a security best practice for storing an Okta API token used by an automation script?
back: Store it in a secrets manager or environment variable injected at runtime, never hard-coded in source control, and scope/rotate it periodically like any other privileged credential.

front: Why convert a legacy script using a static SSWS token to OAuth 2.0 client credentials with API Access Management?
back: It replaces a long-lived, broadly-scoped token with short-lived, narrowly-scoped, independently revocable access tied to a specific service app identity — improving auditability and reducing risk if a credential is ever compromised.

front: What is a Custom Authorization Server in Okta used for?
back: Issuing OAuth 2.0/OIDC access tokens with custom claims, scopes, and access policies tailored to a specific API or set of APIs, distinct from Okta's default org authorization server used for standard sign-in flows.

front: What's the difference between a 'scope' and a 'claim' in API Access Management?
back: A scope defines what permission/resource access is being requested/granted (checked at authorization time to decide what to issue); a claim is a piece of information embedded inside the issued token itself (checked by the resource server at request time).

front: What are the two categories of claims a Custom Authorization Server can include in a token?
back: Built-in/default claims (like sub, iss, exp) that come standard, and custom claims the admin explicitly defines, which can pull from user profile attributes, group membership, or an Okta Expression Language expression.

front: What does an Access Policy on a Custom Authorization Server control?
back: Which client applications are allowed to request tokens from that authorization server, and under what rules (grant type restrictions, scope limits) those requests are evaluated — separate from the broader org-level Authentication Policy.

front: What OAuth 2.0 grant type is most appropriate for a trusted first-party mobile app authenticating its own end user?
back: Authorization Code flow with PKCE — appropriate for any public client (including native mobile apps) needing full user-delegated authorization without exposing a client secret.

front: When might the Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) grant be considered, and why is it discouraged?
back: It might be considered for legacy, highly trusted first-party clients migrating off a direct login form, but it's discouraged because the client handles the user's raw password directly, defeating OAuth's delegated-authorization security model.

front: What's a primary use case for Okta SDKs in the context of API Access Management?
back: Simplifying custom application development by wrapping Okta's REST APIs and OAuth/OIDC token handling (refresh, validation, claims parsing) in idiomatic language-specific libraries instead of hand-rolling raw HTTP calls.

front: What's a common API Access Management use case involving multiple Custom Authorization Servers?
back: Issuing differently-scoped tokens for genuinely distinct APIs or audiences (e.g. a partner-facing API vs. an internal API) so each API's resource server only needs to trust and validate tokens meant specifically for it.

front: What does the 'audience' (aud) claim on an access token represent, and why does a resource server check it?
back: It identifies which API/resource server the token is intended for — a resource server should reject a token whose audience doesn't match itself, even if otherwise validly signed, to prevent a token issued for one API being replayed against another.

front: What's an advantage of defining custom scopes rather than relying only on Okta group checks inside the app?
back: Scope-based authorization decisions happen at the token layer and can be enforced consistently by any resource server validating that token, rather than requiring every downstream app to separately query Okta and re-implement group-based logic.

front: What OAuth grant type is designed for machine-to-machine communication where no user is present?
back: Client Credentials grant — the client authenticates using its own credentials (client ID/secret or a signed JWT) to obtain a token scoped to its own service-level permissions.

front: What does an Access Policy rule's 'grant type' restriction typically prevent?
back: A client meant to use only one grant type (e.g. Authorization Code) from also being able to request tokens via a different, potentially less secure grant type (e.g. Implicit or ROPC) against the same authorization server.

front: Why use an Okta SDK's built-in token validation helper instead of manually decoding a JWT?
back: The SDK correctly implements signature verification against Okta's published JWKS, expiration/issuer/audience checks, and key rotation handling — details easy to get subtly wrong (e.g. skipping signature verification) if implemented by hand.
